recipes.name: Lasagna Stuffed Shells
ingredients_raw: 1 (16 ounce) package shredded mozzarella cheese, divided

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).

Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil; stir in pasta shells and return to a boil. Cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, until shells are nearly cooked through but still very firm to the bite, about 5 minutes. Drain well and rinse with cold water.

While shells are cooking, heat a large skillet over medium-high heat; cook and stir beef and onion in the hot skillet until beef is crumbly, evenly browned, and no longer pink. Drain and discard any excess grease. Stir in tomato paste, tomato sauce, salt, oregano, and garlic powder. Bring to a simmer and cook sauce for 5 minutes. Spread 1/2 of the sauce into a 9x13-inch baking dish.

Beat eggs in a large bowl until smooth. Stir in cottage cheese, 3/4 of the mozzarella, Parmesan, parsley, salt, and pepper until well combined. Spoon cheese mixture into cooked pasta shells and place into the prepared baking dish. Pour remaining sauce over filled shells and sprinkle with remaining mozzarella cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until shells are hot in the center and cheese is melted and bubbly, 25 to 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Lasagna Stuffed Shells
raw_recipe.description: These stuffed shells have all the flavor of lasagna, including the savory beef and cheese filling, stuffed into tender pasta, and they're quick to make!

video.description: A crave-worthy dinner that’s simple to assemble and enjoyable for everyone to eat, this shells, cheese and sauce casserole is an easy twist on the classic lasagna. Simply cook up your pasta shells and ground beef with onion, then add tomato pasta and sauce, oregano, garlic powder, eggs, cottage, mozzarella and Parmesan cheeses, and parsley. Bake until cheese is melted, bubbly and tempting, and serve up with a salad and garlic knots for a complete and satisfying meal.

review.reviewBody: This is a good, solid recipe. I made just a few minor changes: sauteed fresh garlic with the meat instead of using garlic powder, added a few extra seasonings, and cut the meat down to one pound. As always, I used a little Ziploc baggy with the corner cut out to pipe the filling into the shells. Hassle free! I prepared this early in the day, refrigerated, then baked for dinner. Turned out great. Thanks :)

I gave this review 4 stars since I had to make changes. I made the changes based ona couple of the reviews. With the changes this receipe was AMAZING. I used fresh onions and minced garlic. I added season salt, basil, oregano, and fresh parsley to my ground turkey. I used 1.5lbs of ground turkey because I don't eat beef. I used part skim Ricotta Cheese instead of cottage cheese. I also didn't boil my shells like others suggested. I stuffed my shells using a ziploc bag to pipe the Ricotta Cheese mixture into the shells then topped the shells with the meat sauce. Also, note that I diluted the meat sauce with dry white cooking wine instead of using water. Topped with remaining Mozzarella and parmsean cheese and covered tightly with foil and baked on 375 for an hour. After the cooking time I turned the stove off and let it sit in the stove for an additional 10 minutes. Came out delicious and perfect. My picky eaters loved it!!!!

I make this frequently. I like the portion sizes so you don't have to cut a lasagna. The only difference I make is I mix the hamburger into the cheese mixture and stuff the shells with that mixture. Everyone thinks it is better when you do't have a mouth full of cheese. I also use ricotta cheese instead of cottage cheese. I have been making it this way for years and I get requests from family to make it.

Yummy! We used ricotta cheese and “meatless” meat from the brand Quorn. Took advice from another review on here about cutting the corner off a ziploc bag to fill the shells and that was a great tidbit it was!
I read the reviews of others and substituted ricotta for cottage. i also added 10 oz frozen/thawed spinach to the cheese stuffing. got 2 pans out of it so i used 2 jars of spaghetti sauce.

I used ricotta like others suggested and did. Also, I cooked the shells for about 3 min and used a freezer bag with the corner cut to stuff the shells (also as suggested). To my sauce I added green pepper and onion, next time I will use clove garlic instead of powder. Wonderful recipe!

Made it with the ricotta cheese and garlic as suggested by others (I would have used garlic anyway; Garlic on everything - I'm not dating ) ; I loved the zip lock corner of the bag tip!! Delicious and will definitely make again.

A good idea with the stuffed shells with the meat mixture on the bottom and top. I subsituted Ricotta and a half of pound of ground chuck mixed with a half of pound of Italian sausage adds more flavor to the meat sauce. The other spices are purely personal likes. I love some fennel in my sauce. I used a jar and half of already prepared sauce and added more mozzarella cheese on the top and COVERED at 375 for 40 minutes. We prefer a wetter pasta and the cheese seems to taste better. Thank You for Sharing. PS Fresh Parsley is a must

We liked these, but made a few changes. I sautèed minced garlic with the meat instead of using garlic powder, and cut the meat down to one pound. I also used my own homemade marinara and completely omitted the cottage cheese because we do not like it. I added extra mozzarella and parmesan to compensate.

Good, solid recipe! However, I substituted the cottage cheese for ricotta and used canned tomato sauce and added a can of diced tomatoes. I also sauteed onions as well as fresh garlic with the ground beef along with some extra seasonings. I will definitely be making this again!

I used ricotta instead of cottage cheese. Also, I had a few shells left that I filled with the meat sauce and mozzarella cheese. They turned out great. The dish was a huge success and leftovers were gone in no time.

I cook often and I love to experiment with recipes. I don't typically make Italian inspired food because I am not a big pasta fan. That being said, when my husband told me that this was one of his favorite dishes I knew I had to try it. Prep time was a little bit underestimated, but the outcome was really tasty. I would try this again and make a few adjustments.

This recipe was amazing, but I didn't use cottage cheese, I used ricota, and believe me, it is so much better with ricota. My picture is just what I had let from feeding a family of 6. The picture might not look the best, but trust me it was an amazing dinner to cook on a cool night ❤️ I made a few changes in the recipe though, I made the tomatoe sauce and paste just regular spaghetti sauce, I made the cottage cheese ricota, and I didn't have any Parmasion 🧀 asiago 🧀 because I didn't have any parmasion 🧀, I also used a few extra seasonings, I used parsly, basil, thyme, and garlic pouder in all. Love you all, have a great night! ❤️
It was great, easy, and quick. I substituted the cottage cheese for ricotta and instead of dried parsley I used chopped green onions.
I also made with the Ricotta cheese. I use spicy sausage. If you are not going to cook the shells and you are adding water, I would suggest leaving it in for an hour. Overall very good.

Perfect as written. I've made it according to directions and it's superb. My rating is based on the recipe as written. I make both the egg/cheese mixture and the beef/sauce mixtures ahead of time (a day ahead, even), and I always add crushed garlic, because ... garlic! To make things a little easier on myself, I often use a jar of pasta sauce instead of the tomato paste/sauce combo the recipe calls for. I put the cheese mixture in a gallon Ziploc and pipe it into the shells that way. Super amazing. I make it often for guests and people LOVE it and beg for the recipe. This is my go-to heavy pasta dish.

I substituted the cottage cheese for ricotta and used jar marinara. I prefer it with the changes that I made. (I did make it previously by the directions.) This is a quick and easy recipe that the whole family loved.
This recipe is so easy and very delicious!!!
I liked it but it was heavy on the tomato paste so I swamped out half the paste for some crushed tomatoes and I also used half hamburger, half Italian sausage.
